title: Das Alphabet und die Laute
scenario: You are giving your name at a language school and need to spell it clearly. You will hear German letter names, connect each letter to a real word, and practice the sounds that are often different from English.

guidedPractice.explanation: The German letter name Jott belongs to J.
Wasser begins with W, pronounced with a /v/ sound.
German Z makes the /ts/ sound at the start of Zeit.
A wie Apfel is a standard spelling model.
Tür contains the rounded front vowel Ü.
ß is called Eszett or scharfes S.
Name is spelled N – A – M – E.

listening.script: Guten Tag. Wie ist Ihr Name? Mein Name ist Amira. Können Sie das bitte buchstabieren? Ja: A – M – I – R – A. Vielen Dank.

questions.prompt: What name does the speaker spell?
questions.explanation: The speaker says A – M – I – R – A.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say individual letters?
questions.explanation: Buchstabieren means to spell a word letter by letter.

speaking.prompt: Say your name, then spell it slowly with German letter names.
speaking.expectedAnswer: Mein Name ist Amira. A – M – I – R – A.

writing.prompt: Write your first name and separate its letters with dashes.
checklist: I wrote every letter in the correct order.
I checked any Ä, Ö, Ü, or ß carefully.
I can say the German name of each letter I wrote.

recap: You can recognize and say the German letter names.
You connected difficult letters such as J, V, W, and Z to real German sounds.
You practiced Ä, Ö, Ü, and ß.
You can spell your name clearly in a real-life situation.

title: Sich vorstellen
scenario: You have just arrived at a German course. You need to greet people, say your name, where you come from, where you live, and ask simple questions politely.

guidedPractice.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: ___ heiße Maria.
guidedPractice.explanation: Ich means I and is used when you introduce yourself.

guidedPractice.prompt: Build the sentence: aus Syrien / komme / ich
guidedPractice.explanation: In a statement, the conjugated verb is in second position.

guidedPractice.prompt: Formal question for a new teacher:
Build the question: du / wo / wohnst
guidedPractice.explanation: W-question word first, verb second, subject third.

listening.script: Hallo, ich heiße Samir. Ich komme aus Marokko und wohne jetzt in Berlin. Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich hier arbeiten möchte.

questions.explanation: He says: ich wohne jetzt in Berlin.

questions.answer: because he wants to work here
questions.explanation: He says: weil ich hier arbeiten möchte.

speaking.prompt: Introduce yourself in three sentences: name, origin, current city.
speaking.expectedAnswer: Ich heiße Samir. Ich komme aus Marokko. Ich wohne in Berlin.

writing.prompt: Write 1-3 German sentences introducing yourself to a course partner.
checklist: I wrote my city with in.
My conjugated verb is in second position.

recap: You can introduce yourself with ich heiße, ich komme aus, and ich wohne in.
You practiced formal and informal questions.
Four new words are ready for spaced repetition.

title: Im Café bestellen
scenario: You are in a café and want to order politely, ask for the bill, and understand simple prices or service phrases.

guidedPractice.explanation: Kaffee is masculine and becomes einen in the accusative.
Ich möchte is the polite A1 phrase for I would like.

guidedPractice.prompt: Build: bitte / die Rechnung / ich möchte

guidedPractice.explanation: Brot is neuter, so ein stays ein.

listening.script: Guten Morgen. Ich möchte einen Kaffee und ein Brot, bitte. Das macht vier Euro zwanzig.

questions.explanation: They say: einen Kaffee und ein Brot.

speaking.prompt: Order a coffee and ask to pay.
speaking.expectedAnswer: Ich möchte einen Kaffee, bitte. Ich möchte bezahlen.

writing.prompt: Write a short café order with bitte.

recap: You ordered politely with ich möchte.
You practiced masculine accusative with einen Kaffee.
Café words were added to review.
